verdicts.title: Applications of Monotone Rank to Complexity Theory
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Raz's recent result \cite{Raz2010} has rekindled people's interest in the study of \emph{tensor rank}, the generalization of matrix rank to high dimensions, by showing its connections to arithmetic formulas. In this paper, we follow Raz's work and show that \emph{monotone rank}, the monotone variant of tensor rank and matrix rank, has applications in algebraic complexity, quantum computing and communication complexity. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses monotone rank applications to algebraic complexity, quantum correlations, and a multiparty generalization of the log-rank conjecture in deterministic communication complexity — it makes no claim about Geometric Langlands duality or about randomized communication complexity tracking the rank of Langlands dual objects.

verdicts.title: Between Coherent and Constructible Local Langlands Correspondences
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Refined forms of the local Langlands correspondence seek to relate representations of reductive groups over local fields with sheaves on stacks of Langlands parameters. But what kind of sheaves? Conjectures in the spirit of Kazhdan-Lusztig theory (due to Vogan and Soergel) describe representations of a group and its pure inner forms with fixed central character in terms of constructible sheaves. verdicts.title: Langlands Program, Trace Formulas, and their Geometrization
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The Langlands Program relates Galois representations and automorphic representations of reductive algebraic groups. The trace formula is a powerful tool in the study of this connection and the Langlands Functoriality Conjecture. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses the Langlands Program, trace formulas, and their geometrization in the context of Galois representations and automorphic representations of reductive algebraic groups, with no mention of Boolean functions, communication complexity, or any computational/rank correspondence to R(f).
